1	/**
     2	 * Rendezvous (control) socket CLIENT — supervisor side.
     3	 *
     4	 * 1:1 port of ant 5016.js `naK`. The daemon's WorkerVm opens one of these
     5	 * against each worker's rendezvous socket (`<jobDir>/rv.sock`). It is the
     6	 * out-of-band control channel, SEPARATE from the PTY data socket:
     7	 *
     8	 *   - PTY socket  (ptyHost/ptyAdopter): screen bytes, attach/replay.
     9	 *   - rv socket   (this + rvServer):    authoritative state/done/heartbeat
    10	 *                                       pushed by the inner REPL, plus
    11	 *                                       supervisor→worker shutdown/repaint/
    12	 *                                       reply/attacher-caps.
    13	 *
    14	 * Connection model (ant naK, verbatim):
    15	 *   - On construction, connect immediately.
    16	 *   - On connect: reset attempt counter, send the handshake frame
    17	 *     `{ proto, role: 'supervisor', supervisorPid }`, then read newline-
    18	 *     delimited JSON frames and forward each typed message to `onMessage`.
    19	 *   - On close of an ESTABLISHED connection: call `onDisconnect` (the
    20	 *     WorkerVm uses this to immediately re-check the worker pid), then
    21	 *     schedule a reconnect.
    22	 *   - Reconnect backoff: `[100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000]` ms (clamped to the
    23	 *     last entry), capped at 30 attempts. After exhaustion, log
    24	 *     `tengu_bg_rv_connect_exhausted` and stop — the WorkerVm's pid-poll is
    25	 *     the liveness backstop from that point on (rv is an optimisation over
    26	 *     pid-poll, never the only signal).
    27	 *   - `send()`: if there's no live socket and we'd exhausted, reset the
    28	 *     counter and retry (a send is evidence the supervisor still cares
    29	 *     about this worker). Returns false when the frame couldn't be written.
    30	 *
    31	 * Wire framing matches the rest of the daemon protocol (socketProto.ts):
    32	 * one JSON object per line, `\n`-terminated. The handshake carries a
    33	 * `role` field; the server (rvServer.ts) discards any frame that has one,
    34	 * so the handshake is a pure marker and never reaches the worker's
    35	 * command handler (ant kb3: `if("role"in _)return`).
    36	 *
    37	 * @dynamicRequire
    38	 */
    39	
    40	import { Socket } from 'node:net'
    41	
    42	import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'
    43	
    44	import { PROTO_VERSION, createLineDecoder, encodeFrame } from './socketProto.js'
    45	
    46	/**
    47	 * Messages the worker's rv server pushes to the supervisor. Mirrors ant
    48	 * 4291.js `no({type:...})` sends + the 5017.js `connectRv` onMessage
    49	 * dispatch. The supervisor only ever ACTS on these five `type`s; unknown
    50	 * types are ignored (forward-compatible).
    51	 */
    52	export type RvServerMessage =
    53	  | { type: 'heartbeat' }
    54	  | { type: 'done'; outcome: 'done' | 'crashed' | 'killed' }
    55	  | { type: 'state'; patch: Record<string, unknown> }
    56	  | { type: 'detach-request'; msg?: string }
    57	  | { type: 'repaint-done' }
    58	  | { type: 'shutting-down' }
    59	
    60	/**
    61	 * Messages the supervisor sends to the worker. Mirrors ant 5017.js
    62	 * `this.rv.send({type:...})` calls + the 4291.js `kb3` handler.
    63	 */
    64	export type RvClientMessage =
    65	  | { type: 'shutdown' }
    66	  | { type: 'repaint' }
    67	  | { type: 'reply'; text: string }
    68	  | { type: 'attacher-caps'; caps: unknown }
    69	
    70	export interface RvClient {
    71	  /** Send a control frame to the worker. Returns false if not deliverable. */
    72	  send(msg: RvClientMessage): boolean
    73	  /** Tear down: stop reconnecting + destroy the socket. */
    74	  close(): void
    75	}
    76	
    77	/** ant naK backoff (`daK`, assigned in 5017.js iaK init). */
    78	const RV_BACKOFF_MS = [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000] as const
    79	/** ant naK max attempts (`caK = 30`). */
    80	const RV_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 30
    81	
    82	/**
    83	 * Open a rendezvous client against `socketPath`.
    84	 *
    85	 * @param socketPath   the worker's rv.sock path
    86	 * @param onMessage    invoked per typed frame the worker pushes
    87	 * @param onDisconnect invoked whenever an ESTABLISHED connection drops
    88	 *                     (ant `q`) — the WorkerVm wires this to checkPid()
    89	 * @param onConnect    invoked on each successful (re)connect (ant `K`) —
    90	 *                     the WorkerVm wires this to mark workerReady + flush a
    91	 *                     deferred resize + (re)send attacher-caps
    92	 */
    93	export function createRvClient(
    94	  socketPath: string,
    95	  onMessage: (msg: RvServerMessage) => void,
    96	  onDisconnect: () => void,
    97	  onConnect: () => void,
    98	): RvClient {
    99	  let socket: Socket | undefined
   100	  let closed = false
   101	  let attempt = 0
   102	  let gaveUp = false
   103	  let reconnectTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined
   104	
   105	  /** ant `Y` — open one connection attempt. */
   106	  function tryConnect(): void {
   107	    if (closed) return
   108	    const sock = new Socket()
   109	    let opened = false
   110	    sock.on('error', () => scheduleReconnect())
   111	    sock.once('close', () => {
   112	      if (socket === sock) socket = undefined
   113	      if (closed) return
   114	      // Only fire onDisconnect when the connection had actually opened —
   115	      // a never-opened socket just retries (ant: `if(J)q()`).
   116	      if (opened) onDisconnect()
   117	      scheduleReconnect()
   118	    })
   119	    sock.once('connect', () => {
   120	      opened = true
   121	      attempt = 0
   122	      gaveUp = false
   123	      socket = sock
   124	      onConnect()
   125	      // Handshake — `role` marks this frame as supervisor-side so the
   126	      // worker's command handler discards it (ant kb3 `if("role"in _)return`).
   127	      try {
   128	        sock.write(
   129	          encodeFrame({
   130	            proto: PROTO_VERSION,
   131	            role: 'supervisor',
   132	            supervisorPid: process.pid,
   133	          }),
   134	        )
   135	      } catch {
   136	        // best-effort — a write failure here triggers close/error → retry.
   137	      }
   138	      const decode = createLineDecoder(
   139	        msg => {
   140	          if (msg && typeof msg === 'object' && 'type' in msg) {
   141	            onMessage(msg as RvServerMessage)
   142	          }
   143	        },
   144	        () => sock.destroy(),
   145	      )
   146	      sock.on('data', decode)
   147	    })
   148	    sock.connect(socketPath)
   149	  }
   150	
   151	  /** ant `w` — schedule the next reconnect with backoff, or give up. */
   152	  function scheduleReconnect(): void {
   153	    if (closed || reconnectTimer || gaveUp) return
   154	    if (attempt >= RV_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
   155	      gaveUp = true
   156	      logEvent('tengu_bg_rv_connect_exhausted', { attempts: String(attempt) })
   157	      return
   158	    }
   159	    const delay = RV_BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(attempt, RV_BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)]!
   160	    attempt++
   161	    reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   162	      reconnectTimer = undefined
   163	      tryConnect()
   164	    }, delay)
   165	    reconnectTimer.unref()
   166	  }
   167	
   168	  tryConnect()
   169	
   170	  return {
   171	    send(msg: RvClientMessage): boolean {
   172	      if (!socket || socket.destroyed) {
   173	        // A send means the supervisor still cares — if we'd given up,
   174	        // reset and kick a fresh reconnect cycle (ant naK send()).
   175	        if (attempt >= RV_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
   176	          attempt = 0
   177	          gaveUp = false
   178	          scheduleReconnect()
   179	        }
   180	        return false
   181	      }
   182	      try {
   183	        socket.write(encodeFrame(msg))
   184	        return true
   185	      } catch (e) {
   186	        logEvent('tengu_bg_rv_send_failed', { error: String(e).slice(0, 80) })
   187	        return false
   188	      }
   189	    },
   190	    close(): void {
   191	      closed = true
   192	      if (reconnectTimer) {
   193	        clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)
   194	        reconnectTimer = undefined
   195	      }
   196	      socket?.destroy()
   197	      socket = undefined
   198	    },
   199	  }
   200	}

    98	): RvClient {

   103	  let reconnectTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined

   108	    const sock = new Socket()
   109	    let opened = false
   110	    sock.on('error', () => scheduleReconnect())
   111	    sock.once('close', () => {
   112	      if (socket === sock) socket = undefined
   113	      if (closed) return

   115	      // a never-opened socket just retries (ant: `if(J)q()`).
   116	      if (opened) onDisconnect()
   117	      scheduleReconnect()
   118	    })

   120	      opened = true
   121	      attempt = 0
   122	      gaveUp = false
   123	      socket = sock

   126	      // worker's command handler discards it (ant kb3 `if("role"in _)return`).

   129	          encodeFrame({
   130	            proto: PROTO_VERSION,
   131	            role: 'supervisor',
   132	            supervisorPid: process.pid,
   133	          }),
   134	        )
   135	      } catch {

   137	      }

   139	        msg => {
   140	          if (msg && typeof msg === 'object' && 'type' in msg) {
   141	            onMessage(msg as RvServerMessage)
   142	          }
   143	        },
   144	        () => sock.destroy(),
   145	      )

   147	    })

   149	  }

   158	    }

   162	      reconnectTimer = undefined
   163	      tryConnect()
   164	    }, delay)
   165	    reconnectTimer.unref()
   166	  }

   168	  tryConnect()

   174	        // reset and kick a fresh reconnect cycle (ant naK send()).

   178	          scheduleReconnect()
   179	        }
   180	        return false
   181	      }

   185	      } catch (e) {
   186	        logEvent('tengu_bg_rv_send_failed', { error: String(e).slice(0, 80) })
   187	        return false
   188	      }
   189	    },
   190	    close(): void {
   191	      closed = true
   192	      if (reconnectTimer) {
   193	        clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)
   194	        reconnectTimer = undefined
   195	      }
   196	      socket?.destroy()
   197	      socket = undefined
   198	    },
   199	  }
   200	}

1	/**
     2	 * PTY socket adopter — speaks the bg-pty-host wire protocol.
     3	 *
     4	 * Daemon-less ccb's `ccb attach <short>` opens this directly against
     5	 * the PTY host's socket; a future Phase C+ daemon would also use it
     6	 * for cross-process supervision. Mirrors ant 4704.js rj6, but trimmed
     7	 * down: ccb has no daemon supervisor so the respawn-detection /
     8	 * upgrade-tracking / roster-hooks branches are removed. What's kept:
     9	 *
    10	 *   - Connect with backoff (WXK=30 attempts, PXK=[100,250,500,1000,2000])
    11	 *   - ENOENT detection (socket file gone) → caller-visible error
    12	 *   - Hello-handshake receipt (capture replPid + version)
    13	 *   - Buffer queue while disconnected (cap 2MB before drop)
    14	 *   - Per-client backpressure: writableLength > 1 MiB → destroy
    15	 *   - onData / onExit pub-sub callbacks
    16	 *   - write / resize / kill / dispose API surface
    17	 *   - SIGKILL escalation 5s after SIGTERM
    18	 *
    19	 * @dynamicRequire
    20	 */
    21	
    22	import { type Socket, connect } from 'node:net'
    23	
    24	import {
    25	  CTRL_TAG,
    26	  DATA_TAG,
    27	  type CtrlFrame,
    28	  createFrameDecoder,
    29	  encodeCtrlFrame,
    30	  encodeDataFrame,
    31	  FRAME_SIZE_CAP,
    32	} from './ptyFrame.js'
    33	
    34	const RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS = [100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000] as const
    35	const MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 30
    36	const QUEUE_CAP_BYTES = 2 * FRAME_SIZE_CAP // 2 * qiH = 2 MiB
    37	const CLIENT_BACKPRESSURE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
    38	const SIGTERM_GRACE_MS = 5000
    39	
    40	export interface PtyAdopter {
    41	  /** Currently-known REPL pid (from hello frame). 0 if not yet seen. */
    42	  replPid(): number
    43	  /** Currently-known REPL version (from hello frame). '' if not yet seen. */
    44	  replVersion(): string
    45	  /** Send raw bytes to the PTY (will be decoded as user input). Takes a
    46	   *  Buffer, NOT a string: stdin bytes (esp. multi-byte UTF-8 like CJK) must
    47	   *  pass through verbatim. A string round-trip (toString('binary') at the
    48	   *  caller + Buffer.from(s,'utf8') here) double-encoded high bytes and
    49	   *  corrupted CJK input. */
    50	  write(b: Buffer): void
    51	  /** Send a resize ctrl frame. */
    52	  resize(cols: number, rows: number): void
    53	  /** Send a kill ctrl frame. SIGTERM auto-escalates to SIGKILL after 5s. */
    54	  kill(sig: 'SIGTERM' | 'SIGKILL'): void
    55	  /** Tear down the adopter (closes socket, cancels timers). */
    56	  dispose(): void
    57	  /** Subscribe to PTY output (bytes from the host). */
    58	  onData(cb: (chunk: Buffer) => void): { dispose: () => void }
    59	  /** Subscribe to host exit notification. */
    60	  onExit(
    61	    cb: (info: { exitCode: number; signal?: string }) => void,
    62	  ): { dispose: () => void }
    63	  /** Subscribe to host heartbeat ctrl-frames (every 5s while alive). */
    64	  onHeartbeat(cb: (info: { ts: number; state?: string }) => void): { dispose: () => void }
    65	}
    66	
    67	interface AdopterEvent<T> {
    68	  emit(value: T): void
    69	  subscribe(cb: (value: T) => void): () => void
    70	}
    71	
    72	function makeEvent<T>(): AdopterEvent<T> {
    73	  const subs = new Set<(value: T) => void>()
    74	  return {
    75	    emit(value: T): void {
    76	      for (const cb of subs) cb(value)
    77	    },
    78	    subscribe(cb: (value: T) => void): () => void {
    79	      subs.add(cb)
    80	      return () => subs.delete(cb)
    81	    },
    82	  }
    83	}
    84	
    85	/**
    86	 * Open an adopter against the PTY socket at `socketPath`. Returns
    87	 * immediately; the connection happens asynchronously and any data
    88	 * sent via `write/resize/kill` before connect completes is queued.
    89	 */
    90	export function createPtyAdopter(socketPath: string): PtyAdopter {
    91	  const onDataEvent = makeEvent<Buffer>()
    92	  const onExitEvent = makeEvent<{ exitCode: number; signal?: string }>()
    93	  const onHeartbeatEvent = makeEvent<{ ts: number; state?: string }>()
    94	
    95	  let socket: Socket | undefined
    96	  let pendingFrames: Buffer[] = []
    97	  let pendingBytes = 0
    98	  let connected = false
    99	  let disposed = false
   100	  let attempt = 0
   101	  let reconnectTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined
   102	  let drainTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined
   103	  let backpressureTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined
   104	  let sigkillTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined
   105	  let helloPid = 0
   106	  let helloVersion = ''
   107	
   108	  function clearTimers(): void {
   109	    if (drainTimer) {
   110	      clearTimeout(drainTimer)
   111	      drainTimer = undefined
   112	    }
   113	    if (backpressureTimer) {
   114	      clearTimeout(backpressureTimer)
   115	      backpressureTimer = undefined
   116	    }
   117	  }
   118	
   119	  function notifyExit(exitCode: number, signal?: string): void {
   120	    if (disposed) return
   121	    disposed = true
   122	    if (sigkillTimer) {
   123	      clearTimeout(sigkillTimer)
   124	      sigkillTimer = undefined
   125	    }
   126	    clearTimers()
   127	    socket?.destroy()
   128	    socket = undefined
   129	    onExitEvent.emit({ exitCode, signal })
   130	  }
   131	
   132	  function enqueueOrSend(frame: Buffer): void {
   133	    if (socket && !socket.destroyed) {
   134	      const ok = socket.write(frame)
   135	      if (!ok) {
   136	        // backpressure — schedule destroy if drain doesn't fire in 10s
   137	        // (ant XW3 = 10000), and immediate destroy if the buffer crosses
   138	        // CLIENT_BACKPRESSURE_BYTES (ant GXK).
   139	        if (!drainTimer) {
   140	          drainTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   141	            drainTimer = undefined
   142	            socket?.destroy()
   143	          }, 10_000)
   144	          drainTimer.unref()
   145	        }
   146	        if (
   147	          !backpressureTimer &&
   148	          socket.writableLength > CLIENT_BACKPRESSURE_BYTES
   149	        ) {
   150	          backpressureTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   151	            backpressureTimer = undefined
   152	            if (
   153	              socket &&
   154	              !socket.destroyed &&
   155	              socket.writableLength > CLIENT_BACKPRESSURE_BYTES
   156	            ) {
   157	              clearTimers()
   158	              socket.destroy()
   159	            }
   160	          }, 50) // ant PW3 = 50ms grace
   161	          backpressureTimer.unref()
   162	        }
   163	      }
   164	      return
   165	    }
   166	    // Not connected — queue. Drop oldest if over cap.
   167	    if (pendingBytes + frame.length > QUEUE_CAP_BYTES) return
   168	    pendingFrames.push(frame)
   169	    pendingBytes += frame.length
   170	  }
   171	
   172	  function handleFrame(frame: { kind: number; payload?: Buffer; ctrl?: CtrlFrame }): void {
   173	    if (frame.kind === DATA_TAG && frame.payload) {
   174	      onDataEvent.emit(frame.payload)
   175	    } else if (frame.kind === CTRL_TAG && frame.ctrl) {
   176	      const c = frame.ctrl
   177	      if (c.t === 'hello') {
   178	        helloPid = c.replPid
   179	        helloVersion = c.version
   180	      } else if (c.t === 'live') {
   181	        // No-op; live just signals that ring buffer replay is done.
   182	      } else if (c.t === 'exit') {
   183	        notifyExit(c.code, c.signal)
   184	      } else if (c.t === 'heartbeat') {
   185	        onHeartbeatEvent.emit({ ts: c.ts, state: c.state })
   186	      }
   187	    }
   188	  }
   189	
   190	  function tryConnect(): void {
   191	    if (disposed || connected) return
   192	    const sock = connect(socketPath)
   193	    let opened = false
   194	    sock.on('error', err => {
   195	      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') {
   196	        // Socket file is gone — host died or never started.
   197	        // Bubble up as exit so the caller can give up. ant 4704.js:95
   198	        // would retry here; daemon-less ccb has no host to wait for.
   199	        if (!opened) notifyExit(-1, 'ENOENT')
   200	      }
   201	      sock.destroy()
   202	    })
   203	    sock.once('close', () => {
   204	      if (socket === sock) {
   205	        socket = undefined
   206	        connected = false
   207	        clearTimers()
   208	      }
   209	      if (!disposed && !opened) {
   210	        // Connection failed before opening — schedule retry.
   211	        scheduleReconnect()
   212	      }
   213	    })
   214	    sock.once('connect', () => {
   215	      opened = true
   216	      connected = true
   217	      attempt = 0
   218	      socket = sock
   219	      sock.on('drain', clearTimers)
   220	      // Flush queued frames.
   221	      const queued = pendingFrames
   222	      pendingFrames = []
   223	      pendingBytes = 0
   224	      for (const f of queued) enqueueOrSend(f)
   225	    })
   226	    const decoder = createFrameDecoder(handleFrame, () => sock.destroy())
   227	    sock.on('data', decoder)
   228	  }
   229	
   230	  function scheduleReconnect(): void {
   231	    if (disposed || reconnectTimer) return
   232	    if (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS) {
   233	      notifyExit(-1, 'reconnect-exhausted')
   234	      return
   235	    }
   236	    const delay =
   237	      RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(attempt, RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)]!
   238	    attempt++
   239	    reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   240	      reconnectTimer = undefined
   241	      tryConnect()
   242	    }, delay)
   243	    reconnectTimer.unref()
   244	  }
   245	
   246	  // Kick off the initial connection.
   247	  tryConnect()
   248	
   249	  return {
   250	    replPid: () => helloPid,
   251	    replVersion: () => helloVersion,
   252	    write(buf: Buffer): void {
   253	      if (disposed) return
   254	      // Frame body cap is 1 MiB; chunk if larger.
   255	      const chunkSize = FRAME_SIZE_CAP - 1
   256	      for (let i = 0; i < buf.length; i += chunkSize) {
   257	        enqueueOrSend(encodeDataFrame(buf.subarray(i, i + chunkSize)))
   258	      }
   259	    },
   260	    resize(cols: number, rows: number): void {
   261	      if (disposed) return
   262	      enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'resize', cols, rows }))
   263	    },
   264	    kill(sig: 'SIGTERM' | 'SIGKILL'): void {
   265	      if (disposed) return
   266	      enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'kill', sig }))
   267	      if (sig === 'SIGTERM') {
   268	        if (sigkillTimer) clearTimeout(sigkillTimer)
   269	        sigkillTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   270	          sigkillTimer = undefined
   271	          if (!disposed) {
   272	            enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'kill', sig: 'SIGKILL' }))
   273	          }
   274	        }, SIGTERM_GRACE_MS)
   275	        sigkillTimer.unref()
   276	      }
   277	    },
   278	    dispose(): void {
   279	      if (disposed) return
   280	      disposed = true
   281	      if (reconnectTimer) {
   282	        clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)
   283	        reconnectTimer = undefined
   284	      }
   285	      if (sigkillTimer) {
   286	        clearTimeout(sigkillTimer)
   287	        sigkillTimer = undefined
   288	      }
   289	      clearTimers()
   290	      socket?.destroy()
   291	      socket = undefined
   292	    },
   293	    onData(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   294	      const off = onDataEvent.subscribe(cb)
   295	      return { dispose: off }
   296	    },
   297	    onExit(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   298	      const off = onExitEvent.subscribe(cb)
   299	      return { dispose: off }
   300	    },
   301	    onHeartbeat(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   302	      const off = onHeartbeatEvent.subscribe(cb)
   303	      return { dispose: off }
   304	    },
   305	  }
   306	}

   174	      onDataEvent.emit(frame.payload)
   175	    } else if (frame.kind === CTRL_TAG && frame.ctrl) {
   176	      const c = frame.ctrl
   177	      if (c.t === 'hello') {
   178	        helloPid = c.replPid
   179	        helloVersion = c.version
   180	      } else if (c.t === 'live') {
   181	        // No-op; live just signals that ring buffer replay is done.
   182	      } else if (c.t === 'exit') {
   183	        notifyExit(c.code, c.signal)
   184	      } else if (c.t === 'heartbeat') {
   185	        onHeartbeatEvent.emit({ ts: c.ts, state: c.state })
   186	      }
   187	    }
   188	  }
   189	
   190	  function tryConnect(): void {
   191	    if (disposed || connected) return
   192	    const sock = connect(socketPath)
   193	    let opened = false
   194	    sock.on('error', err => {
   195	      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') {
   196	        // Socket file is gone — host died or never started.
   197	        // Bubble up as exit so the caller can give up. ant 4704.js:95
   198	        // would retry here; daemon-less ccb has no host to wait for.
   199	        if (!opened) notifyExit(-1, 'ENOENT')
   200	      }
   201	      sock.destroy()
   202	    })
   203	    sock.once('close', () => {
   204	      if (socket === sock) {
   205	        socket = undefined
   206	        connected = false
   207	        clearTimers()
   208	      }
   209	      if (!disposed && !opened) {
   210	        // Connection failed before opening — schedule retry.
   211	        scheduleReconnect()
   212	      }
   213	    })
   214	    sock.once('connect', () => {
   215	      opened = true
   216	      connected = true
   217	      attempt = 0
   218	      socket = sock
   219	      sock.on('drain', clearTimers)
   220	      // Flush queued frames.
   221	      const queued = pendingFrames
   222	      pendingFrames = []
   223	      pendingBytes = 0
   224	      for (const f of queued) enqueueOrSend(f)
   225	    })
   226	    const decoder = createFrameDecoder(handleFrame, () => sock.destroy())
   227	    sock.on('data', decoder)
   228	  }
   229	
   230	  function scheduleReconnect(): void {
   231	    if (disposed || reconnectTimer) return
   232	    if (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS) {
   233	      notifyExit(-1, 'reconnect-exhausted')
   234	      return
   235	    }
   236	    const delay =
   237	      RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(attempt, RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)]!
   238	    attempt++
   239	    reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   240	      reconnectTimer = undefined
   241	      tryConnect()
   242	    }, delay)
   243	    reconnectTimer.unref()
   244	  }
   245	
   246	  // Kick off the initial connection.
   247	  tryConnect()
   248	
   249	  return {
   250	    replPid: () => helloPid,
   251	    replVersion: () => helloVersion,
   252	    write(buf: Buffer): void {
   253	      if (disposed) return
   254	      // Frame body cap is 1 MiB; chunk if larger.
   255	      const chunkSize = FRAME_SIZE_CAP - 1
   256	      for (let i = 0; i < buf.length; i += chunkSize) {
   257	        enqueueOrSend(encodeDataFrame(buf.subarray(i, i + chunkSize)))
   258	      }
   259	    },
   260	    resize(cols: number, rows: number): void {
   261	      if (disposed) return
   262	      enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'resize', cols, rows }))
   263	    },
   264	    kill(sig: 'SIGTERM' | 'SIGKILL'): void {
   265	      if (disposed) return
   266	      enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'kill', sig }))
   267	      if (sig === 'SIGTERM') {
   268	        if (sigkillTimer) clearTimeout(sigkillTimer)
   269	        sigkillTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   270	          sigkillTimer = undefined
   271	          if (!disposed) {
   272	            enqueueOrSend(encodeCtrlFrame({ t: 'kill', sig: 'SIGKILL' }))
   273	          }
   274	        }, SIGTERM_GRACE_MS)
   275	        sigkillTimer.unref()
   276	      }
   277	    },
   278	    dispose(): void {
   279	      if (disposed) return
   280	      disposed = true
   281	      if (reconnectTimer) {
   282	        clearTimeout(reconnectTimer)
   283	        reconnectTimer = undefined
   284	      }
   285	      if (sigkillTimer) {
   286	        clearTimeout(sigkillTimer)
   287	        sigkillTimer = undefined
   288	      }
   289	      clearTimers()
   290	      socket?.destroy()
   291	      socket = undefined
   292	    },
   293	    onData(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   294	      const off = onDataEvent.subscribe(cb)
   295	      return { dispose: off }
   296	    },
   297	    onExit(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   298	      const off = onExitEvent.subscribe(cb)
   299	      return { dispose: off }
   300	    },
   301	    onHeartbeat(cb): { dispose: () => void } {
   302	      const off = onHeartbeatEvent.subscribe(cb)
   303	      return { dispose: off }
   304	    },
   305	  }
   306	}

1	/**
     2	 * `ccb attach <short>` — interactive bridge to a PTY-mode bg session.
     3	 *
     4	 * Mirrors ant 4649.js aM3 + Yg client side. Connects to the PTY
     5	 * host's Unix socket via `createPtyAdopter`, sets local TTY into raw
     6	 * mode, forwards stdin keystrokes as DATA frames, paints DATA frames
     7	 * back to stdout, and propagates SIGWINCH as resize ctrl frames.
     8	 *
     9	 * Detach key: Ctrl+Q (0x11). Pressing it disposes the adopter and
    10	 * exits the client process WITHOUT killing the bg session — the host
    11	 * keeps running, ready for a future re-attach. This matches ant's
    12	 * detach semantics (clients are decoupled from session lifecycle).
    13	 *
    14	 * Exit code:
    15	 *   0 — clean detach (Ctrl+Q) or session exited normally (code 0)
    16	 *   non-zero — session exited with that code
    17	 *
    18	 * @dynamicRequire
    19	 */
    20	
    21	import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'
    22	import { createDecModeTracker } from './decModeTracker.js'
    23	import { createPtyAdopter, type PtyAdopter } from './ptyAdopter.js'
    24	
    25	const DETACH_KEY_BYTE = 0x11 // Ctrl+Q
    26	/**
    27	 * APC detach sentinel — ant 4176.js `aNH = "\x1b_cc-daemon-detach\x1b\\"`.
    28	 * Emitted by the inner REPL's `$1H()` (4177.js) when the user presses
    29	 * left-arrow on an empty prompt while running as a bg session. runAttach
    30	 * scans incoming PTY data for it, paints any pre-sentinel output, then
    31	 * detaches without killing the bg worker.
    32	 *
    33	 * APC = Application Program Command: ESC `_` <payload> ESC `\` (ST).
    34	 */
    35	const DETACH_APC_SENTINEL = Buffer.from('\x1b_cc-daemon-detach\x1b\\')
    36	
    37	/**
    38	 * `PzH()` equivalent from ant 2281.js — written to stdout when the
    39	 * attach client first connects (and caller is NOT already in alt-screen):
    40	 *   Go_ = \x1b[?1049h   ALT_SCREEN_CLEAR set (enter alt, clear scrollback)
    41	 *   qG  = \x1b[2J       Clear entire screen
    42	 *   _f  = \x1b[H        Move cursor to home
    43	 * (`Fl()` for kitty keyboard is omitted — ccb doesn't ship a kitty kbd
    44	 * protocol decoder, so emitting kitty CSI would corrupt later key parse.)
    45	 */
    46	const ALT_SCREEN_ENTER = '\x1b[?1049h\x1b[2J\x1b[H'
    47	
    48	/**
    49	 * `KE()` equivalent from ant 2281.js — written on detach when not
    50	 * alreadyInAlt:
    51	 *   Ss   = \x1b[<u      disable kitty keyboard protocol  (no-op if not in)
    52	 *   qh9  = \x1b[?1049l  ALT_SCREEN_CLEAR reset (exit alt-screen)
    53	 *   v9H  = \x1b[>4m     disable xterm modifyOtherKeys mode
    54	 */
    55	const ALT_SCREEN_EXIT = '\x1b[<u\x1b[?1049l\x1b[>4m'
    56	
    57	/**
    58	 * Longest-suffix-prefix match. Returns the length `k` such that the last
    59	 * `k` bytes of `buf` equal the first `k` bytes of `needle` — used to
    60	 * detect the start of a sentinel that straddles a chunk boundary.
    61	 *
    62	 * Source: ant 4767.js `Pg8`.
    63	 */
    64	function suffixMatchLen(buf: Buffer, needle: Buffer): number {
    65	  const max = Math.min(buf.length, needle.length - 1)
    66	  outer: for (let k = max; k > 0; k--) {
    67	    const start = buf.length - k
    68	    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    69	      if (buf[start + i] !== needle[i]) continue outer
    70	    }
    71	    return k
    72	  }
    73	  return 0
    74	}
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * Open a PTY socket attach session. Resolves when the bg session
    78	 * exits OR the user presses Ctrl+Q. Caller is responsible for
    79	 * confirming the socket path exists; we'll surface a clear error if
    80	 * connect fails.
    81	 */
    82	export async function runAttach(
    83	  socketPath: string,
    84	  short: string,
    85	): Promise<void> {
    86	  let adopter: PtyAdopter | undefined
    87	  let restoreTty: (() => void) | undefined
    88	  let exitCode = 0
    89	  let detached = false
    90	  const startedAt = Date.now()
    91	  let firstFrameAt = 0
    92	  const decModes = createDecModeTracker()
    93	  logEvent('tengu_bg_attach', { short })
    94	
    95	  // stdin source. Two cases:
    96	  //
    97	  //   (A) Came from in-process FleetView (left-arrow → agents → right-arrow
    98	  //       attach). FleetView destroy()s Bun's process.stdin to give its rust
    99	  //       reader sole ownership of fd 0, so process.stdin is dead here — its
   100	  //       'data'/setRawMode are no-ops. We must read fd 0 through the SAME
   101	  //       rust reader (stdin-napi). Detected via process.stdin.destroyed.
   102	  //
   103	  //   (B) Standalone `ccb attach <short>` from the user's shell. Bun's
   104	  //       process.stdin is alive; use it directly.
   105	  //
   106	  // Both feed the same onData handler below.
   107	  const stdinDestroyed = (process.stdin as NodeJS.ReadStream & {
   108	    destroyed?: boolean
   109	  }).destroyed === true
   110	  let nativeReaderStop: (() => void) | undefined
   111	
   112	  // Local TTY raw-mode setup. Without this, the local terminal would
   113	  // do its own line-buffering + Ctrl+C → SIGINT → kill the attach
   114	  // client's process (which we don't want). Raw mode also lets us
   115	  // detect the Ctrl+Q sentinel. In case (A) the rust reader owns termios,
   116	  // so we skip the Node setRawMode (it would throw on a destroyed stream).
   117	  if (!stdinDestroyed && process.stdin.isTTY && process.stdin.setRawMode) {
   118	    const wasRaw = process.stdin.isRaw
   119	    process.stdin.setRawMode(true)
   120	    restoreTty = () => {
   121	      try {
   122	        if (process.stdin.setRawMode) process.stdin.setRawMode(wasRaw)
   123	      } catch {
   124	        // best-effort
   125	      }
   126	    }
   127	  }
   128	
   129	  // Alt-screen ENTER is handled by the caller (agentsFleet loop) so
   130	  // the swap brackets the unmount-FleetView → spawn-runAttach gap.
   131	  // For the standalone `ccb attach <short>` CLI, the caller is the
   132	  // user's shell and the inner REPL's own alt-screen toggle is what
   133	  // the user sees — we write ALT_SCREEN_ENTER below as a fallback
   134	  // only when stdin/stdout look like a TTY but no caller-managed
   135	  // swap has happened yet (heuristic: `CCB_ATTACH_OWNED_ALT_SCREEN`
   136	  // env set by the loop).
   137	  if (!process.env.CCB_ATTACH_OWNED_ALT_SCREEN) {
   138	    process.stdout.write(ALT_SCREEN_ENTER)
   139	  }
   140	
   141	  // Open adopter against the host socket.
   142	  adopter = createPtyAdopter(socketPath)
   143	
   144	  // Forward local stdin keystrokes to the PTY. Two sources (see stdinDestroyed
   145	  // above): the rust reader (case A — FleetView destroy()d process.stdin) or
   146	  // Bun's process.stdin 'data' event (case B — standalone `ccb attach`). Both
   147	  // feed onData. We use 'data' (flowing), not 'readable'+read(): on public Bun,
   148	  // process.stdin's 'readable' is unreliable for raw-mode keystrokes after an
   149	  // Ink unmount (ant uses 'readable' only because its bun-internal fork patches
   150	  // this). Stop reading local stdin — works for both sources. Idempotent.
   151	  const stopStdin = (): void => {
   152	    if (nativeReaderStop) {
   153	      nativeReaderStop()
   154	      nativeReaderStop = undefined
   155	    } else {
   156	      process.stdin.removeListener('data', onData)
   157	    }
   158	  }
   159	  const handleByteChunk = (chunkBuf: Buffer): void => {
   160	    // Scan for Ctrl+Q. Pass everything before the sentinel through;
   161	    // anything after is dropped because we're detaching.
   162	    const idx = chunkBuf.indexOf(DETACH_KEY_BYTE)
   163	    if (idx === -1) {
   164	      adopter!.write(chunkBuf)
   165	      return
   166	    }
   167	    if (idx > 0) {
   168	      adopter!.write(chunkBuf.subarray(0, idx))
   169	    }
   170	    detached = true
   171	    stopStdin()
   172	  }
   173	  const onData = (chunk: Buffer | string): void => {
   174	    const buf = Buffer.isBuffer(chunk)
   175	      ? chunk
   176	      : Buffer.from(chunk as string, 'utf8')
   177	    handleByteChunk(buf)
   178	  }
   179	  if (stdinDestroyed) {
   180	    // Case (A): read fd 0 through the rust reader (Bun's process.stdin is
   181	    // destroyed by FleetView). The reader owns termios + reads on its own
   182	    // thread, feeding onData with each chunk. redirect_fd0=false: fd 0 is
   183	    // free (Bun no longer reads it), so no dup2 redirect needed.
   184	    const { startReader } = await import('@thyrox/stdin-napi')
   185	    let handle: { stop(): void } | undefined
   186	    try {
   187	      handle = startReader(false, onData)
   188	    } catch {
   189	      // reader failed to start; leave handle undefined (no input forwarding)
   190	    }
   191	    nativeReaderStop = () => {
   192	      try {
   193	        handle?.stop()
   194	      } catch {
   195	        // best-effort
   196	      }
   197	    }
   198	  } else {
   199	    process.stdin.on('data', onData)
   200	    process.stdin.ref()
   201	    process.stdin.resume()
   202	  }
   203	
   204	  // Frame-boundary buffer: hold all incoming PTY bytes until we see
   205	  // the inner REPL emit a frame boundary marker — either:
   206	  //   `\x1b[2J`        clear-entire-screen (legacy full-repaint marker)
   207	  //   `\x1b[H\x1b[2K`  cursor-home + erase-line (ant's `P` sentinel — see
   208	  //                    5288.js daemon attach: `let P = _f + zzH`).
   209	  // Both indicate the start of a complete frame. Until one arrives the
   210	  // alt-screen retains the outer FleetView pixels (preserved by
   211	  // `handoffAltScreen` — see agentsFleet.ts). When one arrives we flush
   212	  // FROM it onwards AND wrap the flush in `BSU…ESU` to force the
   213	  // terminal (when DEC 2026 is supported, e.g. iTerm2) to apply the
   214	  // whole transition atomically — even if the inner's own framing
   215	  // didn't wrap THIS chunk in BSU/ESU. Without DEC 2026 it's a no-op.
   216	  //
   217	  // Source: ant 5288.js attach handler —
   218	  //   if (qH.includes(qG) || qH.includes(P)) { write(qH or r) }
   219	  // where qG=\x1b[2J, P=\x1b[H\x1b[2K, plus the BSU/ESU wrap that ant
   220	  // Ink already inlines around every render (terminal.ts ant equivalent).
   221	  const FRAME_CLEAR = Buffer.from('\x1b[2J')
   222	  const FRAME_HOME_ERASE = Buffer.from('\x1b[H\x1b[2K')
   223	  const BSU = Buffer.from('\x1b[?2026h')
   224	  const ESU = Buffer.from('\x1b[?2026l')
   225	  // Source: ant 4767.js `Md` write logic — line:
   226	  //   K.write(_.alreadyInAlt ? ru + Fl() + YH : PzH() + YH + (m ? ru : "") + ...)
   227	  // When `alreadyInAlt` is true, ant DOES NOT buffer waiting for a
   228	  // frame-boundary marker. It writes the ack DEC modes immediately and
   229	  // then paints incoming PTY bytes the moment they arrive. The trick:
   230	  //
   231	  //   - The alt-screen buffer already has the outer FleetView pixels
   232	  //     (preserved by `handoffAltScreen()` — no \x1b[?1049l was emitted).
   233	  //   - The inner REPL's first paint is INVISIBLE escape codes (DEC
   234	  //     mode sets/resets) until it finally emits its own \x1b[2J or
   235	  //     home-erase as part of its first render. Those invisible codes
   236	  //     change terminal state, not the visible cells.
   237	  //   - When the inner's first render does fire, its CLEAR+CELLS pair
   238	  //     overwrites the FleetView pixels in a single coherent paint.
   239	  //
   240	  // ccb previously buffered everything until a frame-boundary marker
   241	  // appeared, which meant during the inner REPL's boot delay (~1-2s of
   242	  // bun + bundle load + first-render) NOTHING was painted. With proper
   243	  // handoff the alt-screen WOULD still show FleetView pixels — but only
   244	  // if no other write happened. Inner-REPL boot emits non-clearing
   245	  // escape codes that are safely ignored by the terminal; buffering
   246	  // them deferred the natural transition without benefit.
   247	  //
   248	  // Set `attachBuffer = null` initially when CCB_ATTACH_OWNED_ALT_SCREEN
   249	  // is set so we mirror ant exactly (no buffer). Standalone `ccb attach`
   250	  // (no env var) keeps the buffer because runAttach itself wrote
   251	  // `\x1b[?1049h\x1b[2J\x1b[H` and the screen is blank — buffering until
   252	  // first frame avoids painting partial mode-setup garbage.
   253	  const ownedAltScreen = !!process.env.CCB_ATTACH_OWNED_ALT_SCREEN
   254	  let attachBuffer: Buffer | null = ownedAltScreen ? null : Buffer.alloc(0)
   255	
   256	  // Render incoming PTY output to local stdout. Track DEC private modes
   257	  // (ant 4638.js Yg) so detach can restore local terminal state. Also
   258	  // scan for ant's APC detach sentinel (ant 4177.js $1H → 4176.js w_H).
   259	  //
   260	  // Source: ant 4767.js `o(s)` — buffers a partial-match tail across
   261	  // chunk boundaries so the sentinel isn't missed across packets.
   262	  let pendingTail: Buffer = Buffer.alloc(0)
   263	  const handleLivePaint = (incoming: Buffer): void => {
   264	    if (firstFrameAt === 0) {
   265	      firstFrameAt = Date.now()
   266	      logEvent('tengu_bg_attach_first_frame', {
   267	        ms: String(firstFrameAt - startedAt),
   268	      })
   269	    }
   270	    const wH =
   271	      pendingTail.length > 0 ? Buffer.concat([pendingTail, incoming]) : incoming
   272	
   273	    const idx = wH.indexOf(DETACH_APC_SENTINEL)
   274	    if (idx >= 0) {
   275	      if (idx > 0) {
   276	        const before = wH.subarray(0, idx)
   277	        decModes.feed(before)
   278	        process.stdout.write(before)
   279	      }
   280	      pendingTail = Buffer.alloc(0)
   281	      detached = true
   282	      stopStdin()
   283	      return
   284	    }
   285	
   286	    const k = suffixMatchLen(wH, DETACH_APC_SENTINEL)
   287	    if (wH.length > k) {
   288	      const paint = wH.subarray(0, wH.length - k)
   289	      decModes.feed(paint)
   290	      process.stdout.write(paint)
   291	    }
   292	    pendingTail = k > 0 ? Buffer.from(wH.subarray(wH.length - k)) : Buffer.alloc(0)
   293	  }
   294	
   295	  const dataSub = adopter.onData(chunk => {
   296	    const incoming = Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk, 'binary')
   297	
   298	    if (attachBuffer !== null) {
   299	      attachBuffer = Buffer.concat([attachBuffer, incoming])
   300	      const clearIdx = attachBuffer.indexOf(FRAME_CLEAR)
   301	      const homeEraseIdx = attachBuffer.indexOf(FRAME_HOME_ERASE)
   302	      let markerIdx = -1
   303	      if (clearIdx >= 0 && homeEraseIdx >= 0) {
   304	        markerIdx = Math.min(clearIdx, homeEraseIdx)
   305	      } else if (clearIdx >= 0) {
   306	        markerIdx = clearIdx
   307	      } else if (homeEraseIdx >= 0) {
   308	        markerIdx = homeEraseIdx
   309	      }
   310	      if (markerIdx === -1) {
   311	        // No frame boundary yet — keep buffering. Cap at 1 MiB so a
   312	        // misbehaving stream doesn't OOM us.
   313	        if (attachBuffer.length > 1024 * 1024) {
   314	          attachBuffer = attachBuffer.subarray(attachBuffer.length - 1024 * 1024)
   315	        }
   316	        return
   317	      }
   318	      // Found a boundary — flush from it. Wrap in BSU/ESU so terminals
   319	      // supporting DEC 2026 apply the whole `clear+cells` transition
   320	      // atomically (FleetView pixels → session UI with zero
   321	      // intermediate paint). On terminals without sync support the
   322	      // wrap is harmless (BSU/ESU are just unknown DECSET codes).
   323	      const flushBytes = attachBuffer.subarray(markerIdx)
   324	      attachBuffer = null
   325	      handleLivePaint(Buffer.concat([BSU, flushBytes, ESU]))
   326	      return
   327	    }
   328	
   329	    handleLivePaint(incoming)
   330	  })
   331	
   332	  // Resolve when the host signals exit OR we detach.
   333	  const exitPromise = new Promise<void>(resolve => {
   334	    const exitSub = adopter!.onExit(info => {
   335	      exitCode = info.exitCode === -1 ? 1 : info.exitCode
   336	      exitSub.dispose()
   337	      resolve()
   338	    })
   339	  })
   340	
   341	  // Resize propagation: when the local terminal changes size, send
   342	  // a resize ctrl frame so the host PTY matches.
   343	  const initialResize = (): void => {
   344	    const cols = process.stdout.columns
   345	    const rows = process.stdout.rows
   346	    if (cols && rows) adopter!.resize(cols, rows)
   347	  }
   348	  initialResize()
   349	  const onResize = (): void => initialResize()
   350	  process.stdout.on('resize', onResize)
   351	
   352	  // ant 5164.js stall watchdog: if no first frame within
   353	  // NO client-side first-frame/stall watchdog. Source: ant `dc` (4945.js)
   354	  // has none — its only timeout is a 10s ACK timeout cleared the moment the
   355	  // daemon's attach-ack arrives; after that the client never times out on
   356	  // frame data. An idle worker (state.tempo=blocked, "send a prompt to
   357	  // start") sits silent at its prompt and emits no frame, so a client-side
   358	  // "no first frame in 30s → kill" watchdog MISFIRES on idle sessions and
   359	  // tears the whole attach (and process) down at exactly 30s. ant avoids
   360	  // this by (a) keeping stall detection on the DAEMON/host side, gated on
   361	  // "did a forced repaint produce bytes", not on a blind client clock, and
   362	  // (b) forcing the inner REPL to redraw on every attach so a frame always
   363	  // arrives. ccb's host-side repaint-on-attach lives in ptyHost.ts; the
   364	  // client just paints whatever the PTY sends, including nothing.
   365	  // firstFrameAt below is kept for telemetry only (ant's f() does the same).
   366

     3	 *
     4	 * Mirrors ant 4649.js aM3 + Yg client side. Connects to the PTY
     5	 * host's Unix socket via `createPtyAdopter`, sets local TTY into raw
     6	 * mode, forwards stdin keystrokes as DATA frames, paints DATA frames
     7	 * back to stdout, and propagates SIGWINCH as resize ctrl frames.
     8	 *
     9	 * Detach key: Ctrl+Q (0x11). Pressing it disposes the adopter and
    10	 * exits the client process WITHOUT killing the bg session — the host
    11	 * keeps running, ready for a future re-attach. This matches ant's
    12	 * detach semantics (clients are decoupled from session lifecycle).
    13	 *
    14	 * Exit code:
    15	 *   0 — clean detach (Ctrl+Q) or session exited normally (code 0)
    16	 *   non-zero — session exited with that code
    17	 *
    18	 * @dynamicRequire
    19	 */

    21	import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'
    22	import { createDecModeTracker } from './decModeTracker.js'
    23	import { createPtyAdopter, type PtyAdopter } from './ptyAdopter.js'

    25	const DETACH_KEY_BYTE = 0x11 // Ctrl+Q
    26	/**
    27	 * APC detach sentinel — ant 4176.js `aNH = "\x1b_cc-daemon-detach\x1b\\"`.
    28	 * Emitted by the inner REPL's `$1H()` (4177.js) when the user presses
    29	 * left-arrow on an empty prompt while running as a bg session. runAttach
    30	 * scans incoming PTY data for it, paints any pre-sentinel output, then
    31	 * detaches without killing the bg worker.
    32	 *
    33	 * APC = Application Program Command: ESC `_` <payload> ESC `\` (ST).
    34	 */
    35	const DETACH_APC_SENTINEL = Buffer.from('\x1b_cc-daemon-detach\x1b\\')
    36	
    37	/**
    38	 * `PzH()` equivalent from ant 2281.js — written to stdout when the
    39	 * attach client first connects (and caller is NOT already in alt-screen):
    40	 *   Go_ = \x1b[?1049h   ALT_SCREEN_CLEAR set (enter alt, clear scrollback)
    41	 *   qG  = \x1b[2J       Clear entire screen
    42	 *   _f  = \x1b[H        Move cursor to home

    44	 * protocol decoder, so emitting kitty CSI would corrupt later key parse.)
    45	 */

    47

    49	 * `KE()` equivalent from ant 2281.js — written on detach when not
    50	 * alreadyInAlt:

    60	 * detect the start of a sentinel that straddles a chunk boundary.

    68	    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
    69	      if (buf[start + i] !== needle[i]) continue outer
    70	    }
    71	    return k
    72	  }
    73	  return 0
    74	}

    76	/**
    77	 * Open a PTY socket attach session. Resolves when the bg session
    78	 * exits OR the user presses Ctrl+Q. Caller is responsible for
    79	 * confirming the socket path exists; we'll surface a clear error if
    80	 * connect fails.
    81	 */

    83	  socketPath: string,
    84	  short: string,
    85	): Promise<void> {

    87	  let restoreTty: (() => void) | undefined
    88	  let exitCode = 0
    89	  let detached = false
    90	  const startedAt = Date.now()
    91	  let firstFrameAt = 0
    92	  const decModes = createDecModeTracker()
    93	  logEvent('tengu_bg_attach', { short })
    94	
    95	  // stdin source. Two cases:
    96	  //
    97	  //   (A) Came from in-process FleetView (left-arrow → agents → right-arrow
    98	  //       attach). FleetView destroy()s Bun's process.stdin to give its rust
    99	  //       reader sole ownership of fd 0, so process.stdin is dead here — its
   100	  //       'data'/setRawMode are no-ops. We must read fd 0 through the SAME
   101	  //       rust reader (stdin-napi). Detected via process.stdin.destroyed.
   102	  //
   103	  //   (B) Standalone `ccb attach <short>` from the user's shell. Bun's
   104	  //       process.stdin is alive; use it directly.
   105	  //
   106	  // Both feed the same onData handler below.
   107	  const stdinDestroyed = (process.stdin as NodeJS.ReadStream & {
   108	    destroyed?: boolean

   110	  let nativeReaderStop: (() => void) | undefined
   111

   115	  // detect the Ctrl+Q sentinel. In case (A) the rust reader owns termios,

   118	    const wasRaw = process.stdin.isRaw
   119	    process.stdin.setRawMode(true)

   121	      try {
   122	        if (process.stdin.setRawMode) process.stdin.setRawMode(wasRaw)
   123	      } catch {
   124	        // best-effort
   125	      }
   126	    }
   127	  }
   128	
   129	  // Alt-screen ENTER is handled by the caller (agentsFleet loop) so
   130	  // the swap brackets the unmount-FleetView → spawn-runAttach gap.
   131	  // For the standalone `ccb attach <short>` CLI, the caller is the
   132	  // user's shell and the inner REPL's own alt-screen toggle is what

   136	  // env set by the loop).

   142	  adopter = createPtyAdopter(socketPath)
   143	
   144	  // Forward local stdin keystrokes to the PTY. Two sources (see stdinDestroyed
   145	  // above): the rust reader (case A — FleetView destroy()d process.stdin) or
   146	  // Bun's process.stdin 'data' event (case B — standalone `ccb attach`). Both
   147	  // feed onData. We use 'data' (flowing), not 'readable'+read(): on public Bun,
   148	  // process.stdin's 'readable' is unreliable for raw-mode keystrokes after an
   149	  // Ink unmount (ant uses 'readable' only because its bun-internal fork patches

   153	      nativeReaderStop()
   154	      nativeReaderStop = undefined
   155	    } else {

   157	    }
   158	  }

   172	  }

   217	  // Source: ant 5288.js attach handler —

   232	  //     (preserved by `handoffAltScreen()` — no \x1b[?1049l was emitted).

   279	      }

   291	    }

   293	  }

   301	      const homeEraseIdx = attachBuffer.indexOf(FRAME_HOME_ERASE)

   303	      if (clearIdx >= 0 && homeEraseIdx >= 0) {
   304	        markerIdx = Math.min(clearIdx, homeEraseIdx)
   305	      } else if (clearIdx >= 0) {
   306	        markerIdx = clearIdx
   307	      } else if (homeEraseIdx >= 0) {

   309	      }

   367	  // Wait for either exit or detach.

   386	  // Alt-screen EXIT — only when we own the swap (standalone CLI).

   406	    got_first_frame: String(firstFrameAt > 0),

   408	  })

   411	  // RETURN — process.exit would kill the outer FleetView too. The

   413	  // attachHandler and exits cleanly. Detach/exit reasons are surfaced
   414	  // via the returned outcome string so callers can decide.
   415	  if (detached) {
   416	    process.stderr.write(`\n[detached from ${short} — session keeps running]\n`)

   418	  }
   419	  process.stderr.write(`\n[session ${short} exited with code ${exitCode}]\n`)

1	/**
     2	 * Daemon socket wire protocol.
     3	 *
     4	 * Envelope: each request and response is a single JSON object followed
     5	 * by a `\n` terminator. ant 4138.js uses the same format (line 64-67:
     6	 * `EH(H) + "\n"`).
     7	 *
     8	 * Protocol version: ant uses `proto: W5` where W5 is a constant that
     9	 * gets bumped on breaking changes. ccb mirrors as `PROTO_VERSION` =
    10	 * 1 for now; we'll bump if we change framing semantics.
    11	 *
    12	 * Op codes (CLI → Daemon unless noted):
    13	 *   ping            — liveness check
    14	 *   nudge           — poll daemon restart state (returns {restarting})
    15	 *   list            — enumerate active workers
    16	 *   spawn           — create new bg session (with dispatch envelope)
    17	 *   dispatch        — alt dispatch path; takes nonce + spool file
    18	 *   await-ack       — wait for spawn/dispatch ACK by nonce
    19	 *   subscribe       — stream worker output (snapshot + delta)
    20	 *   attach          — open per-job claim socket (handshake to PTY)
    21	 *   resize          — propagate window resize from client
    22	 *   kill            — signal worker; returns {confirmed: bool}
    23	 *   respawn         — kill + restart same short id
    24	 *   retire          — schedule retire after idleGracePeriodMs
    25	 *   shutdown        — graceful daemon shutdown
    26	 *   reply           — send text input to a blocked worker
    27	 *   attacher-caps   — advertise client capabilities
    28	 *   lease           — keepalive heartbeat from CLI client
    29	 *
    30	 * Plus daemon-side worker → daemon ops (forward-only):
    31	 *   heartbeat, state, done, detach-request
    32	 *
    33	 * @dynamicRequire
    34	 */
    35	
    36	export const PROTO_VERSION = 1
    37	
    38	export type ProtoOp =
    39	  | 'ping'
    40	  | 'nudge'
    41	  | 'list'
    42	  | 'spawn'
    43	  | 'dispatch'
    44	  | 'await-ack'
    45	  | 'subscribe'
    46	  | 'attach'
    47	  | 'resize'
    48	  | 'kill'
    49	  | 'respawn'
    50	  | 'retire'
    51	  | 'shutdown'
    52	  | 'reply'
    53	  | 'sendclaim'
    54	  | 'respawn-stalled'
    55	  | 'detach'
    56	  | 'yield'
    57	  | 'attacher-caps'
    58	  | 'lease'
    59	
    60	export interface BaseRequest {
    61	  proto: number
    62	  op: ProtoOp
    63	}
    64	
    65	export interface OkResponse {
    66	  ok: true
    67	  op?: ProtoOp
    68	  [k: string]: unknown
    69	}
    70	
    71	export interface ErrorResponse {
    72	  ok: false
    73	  code:
    74	    | 'ENOCONN'
    75	    | 'ETIMEOUT'
    76	    | 'ENOJOB'
    77	    | 'ESTALE'
    78	    | 'EALIVE'
    79	    | 'EBUSY'
    80	    | 'EBADREQ'
    81	    | 'EUNSUPPORTED'
    82	    | string
    83	  error: string
    84	  [k: string]: unknown
    85	}
    86	
    87	export type Response = OkResponse | ErrorResponse
    88	
    89	/** Encode a request/response as the wire envelope (JSON + LF). */
    90	export function encodeFrame(obj: object): string {
    91	  return `${JSON.stringify(obj)}\n`
    92	}
    93	
    94	/**
    95	 * Per-line overflow guard. ant 4291.js's rv server caps its inbound
    96	 * buffer at 1 MiB (`if(q.length>1048576)q="",_.destroy()`) so a peer that
    97	 * never sends a newline can't grow the pending buffer without bound. Legit
    98	 * protocol frames (RPC envelopes, rv control frames) are tiny JSON lines
    99	 * far under this, so the cap only ever trips on a wedged/hostile peer.
   100	 */
   101	const MAX_PENDING_LINE_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
   102	
   103	/**
   104	 * Stateful line decoder for socket data. Calls `onMessage` once per
   105	 * complete `\n`-terminated JSON line; calls `onError` and stops on
   106	 * malformed input or on a single line exceeding MAX_PENDING_LINE_BYTES.
   107	 */
   108	export function createLineDecoder(
   109	  onMessage: (msg: unknown) => void,
   110	  onError: (msg: string) => void,
   111	): (chunk: string | Buffer) => void {
   112	  let buf = ''
   113	  let stopped = false
   114	  return (chunk: string | Buffer) => {
   115	    if (stopped) return
   116	    buf += typeof chunk === 'string' ? chunk : chunk.toString('utf8')
   117	    while (true) {
   118	      const idx = buf.indexOf('\n')
   119	      if (idx < 0) {
   120	        // No complete line yet — bound the pending buffer (ant 4291.js).
   121	        if (buf.length > MAX_PENDING_LINE_BYTES) {
   122	          stopped = true
   123	          buf = ''
   124	          onError(
   125	            `protocol line exceeds ${MAX_PENDING_LINE_BYTES} bytes without terminator`,
   126	          )
   127	        }
   128	        return
   129	      }
   130	      const line = buf.slice(0, idx)
   131	      buf = buf.slice(idx + 1)
   132	      if (line.length === 0) continue
   133	      try {
   134	        onMessage(JSON.parse(line))
   135	      } catch (err) {
   136	        stopped = true
   137	        onError(`bad protocol line: ${(err as Error).message}`)
   138	        return
   139	      }
   140	    }
   141	  }
   142	}

   113	  let stopped = false

   115	    if (stopped) return

   126	          )
   127	        }
   128	        return
   129	      }

   131	      buf = buf.slice(idx + 1)

   133	      try {
   134	        onMessage(JSON.parse(line))
   135	      } catch (err) {
   136	        stopped = true
   137	        onError(`bad protocol line: ${(err as Error).message}`)

   139	      }

1	/**
     2	 * El códec de trama del socket entre el anfitrión de PTY y sus clientes.
     3	 *
     4	 * Un socket entrega bytes, no mensajes: dos escrituras pueden llegar en un
     5	 * trozo y una escritura puede llegar en cinco. El códec es lo que devuelve la
     6	 * frontera del mensaje, y su forma es la mínima que lo consigue —longitud por
     7	 * delante, y una etiqueta que dice cómo leer el cuerpo:
     8	 *
     9	 *   ┌────────────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────────┐
    10	 *   │ 4 B longitud (BE)  │ 1 B etiqueta  │ cuerpo de N B    │
    11	 *   └────────────────────┴───────────────┴──────────────────┘
    12	 *
    13	 *   etiqueta 0 (DATA_TAG) — el cuerpo son bytes crudos: salida o entrada
    14	 *                           del PTY, que NO se interpretan
    15	 *   etiqueta 1 (CTRL_TAG) — el cuerpo es JSON en utf-8, con `t` de tipo
    16	 *
    17	 * Por qué la longitud va PRIMERO y en big-endian: primero, porque el lector
    18	 * necesita saber cuánto esperar antes de poder esperar; big-endian porque es
    19	 * el orden de red y lo que `readUInt32BE` da sin conversión.
    20	 *
    21	 * Por qué los datos crudos NO pasan por JSON: la salida de un PTY es binaria
    22	 * —secuencias de escape, UTF-8 a medias en la frontera de un trozo— y
    23	 * envolverla en JSON obligaría a escaparla y a re-parsearla en cada trozo, que
    24	 * es coste por byte sobre el camino más caliente del protocolo. La etiqueta
    25	 * separa los dos regímenes y deja el caro sólo para el control, que es raro.
    26	 *
    27	 * Adaptación del patrón de `ccnmt: packages/cli/src/bg/ptyFrame.ts`. NO es
    28	 * copia de su texto: ccnmt declara `"license": "UNLICENSED"` (#207).
    29	 */
    30	
    31	/** El cuerpo son bytes crudos, sin interpretar. */
    32	export const DATA_TAG = 0
    33	/** El cuerpo es JSON en utf-8. */
    34	export const CTRL_TAG = 1
    35	/** Longitud (4 B) + etiqueta (1 B). */
    36	export const FRAME_HEADER_BYTES = 5
    37	/** Tope del búfer circular de reenganche — ver `ptyRing.ts`. */
    38	export const RING_BUFFER_BYTES = 256 * 1024
    39	/**
    40	 * Tope del cuerpo de una trama, INCLUSIVE: un cuerpo de exactamente este
    41	 * tamaño es válido. Existe para que una longitud corrupta no haga reservar
    42	 * gigabytes antes de descubrir que la trama era basura.
    43	 */
    44	export const FRAME_SIZE_CAP = 1024 * 1024
    45	
    46	/**
    47	 * Las tramas de control, por sentido:
    48	 *
    49	 *   `hello`     anfitrión → cliente, al conectar
    50	 *   `live`      anfitrión → cliente, terminó la reproducción del búfer
    51	 *   `exit`      anfitrión → cliente, el hijo terminó
    52	 *   `heartbeat` anfitrión → cliente, sigue vivo
    53	 *   `resize`    cliente → anfitrión, cambia el tamaño del PTY
    54	 *   `kill`      cliente → anfitrión, manda una señal
    55	 *   `detach`    sesión bg → anfitrión, pide soltar a los clientes
    56	 *               (`bgDetachSignal.ts`; lo atiende `ptyHost.handleCtrl`)
    57	 *   `claim`     demonio → trabajador de reserva, le entrega la intención
    58	 *   `reply`     demonio → trabajador, encola texto como próximo turno
    59	 */
    60	export type CtrlFrame =
    61	  | { t: 'hello'; replPid: number; version: string }
    62	  | { t: 'live' }
    63	  | { t: 'exit'; code: number; signal?: string }
    64	  | { t: 'resize'; cols: number; rows: number }
    65	  | { t: 'kill'; sig: 'SIGKILL' | 'SIGTERM' }
    66	  | { t: 'detach' }
    67	  | { t: 'claim'; intent: string; cwd?: string; sessionId?: string }
    68	  | { t: 'reply'; text: string }
    69	  | { t: 'heartbeat'; ts: number; state?: string }
    70	
    71	export type DecodedFrame =
    72	  | { kind: typeof DATA_TAG; payload: Buffer }
    73	  | { kind: typeof CTRL_TAG; ctrl: CtrlFrame }
    74	
    75	/** Arma una trama con su cabecera. */
    76	function frame(tag: number, body: Buffer): Buffer {
    77	  const out = Buffer.allocUnsafe(FRAME_HEADER_BYTES + body.length)
    78	  out.writeUInt32BE(body.length, 0)
    79	  out.writeUInt8(tag, 4)
    80	  body.copy(out, FRAME_HEADER_BYTES)
    81	  return out
    82	}
    83	
    84	/** Envuelve bytes crudos en una trama de datos. */
    85	export function encodeDataFrame(payload: Buffer | string): Buffer {
    86	  return frame(DATA_TAG, typeof payload === 'string' ? Buffer.from(payload, 'utf8') : payload)
    87	}
    88	
    89	/** Envuelve un objeto de control en su trama. */
    90	export function encodeCtrlFrame(ctrl: CtrlFrame): Buffer {
    91	  return frame(CTRL_TAG, Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(ctrl), 'utf8'))
    92	}
    93	
    94	/**
    95	 * Un decodificador con estado: acepta trozos del socket y llama a `onFrame`
    96	 * por cada trama completa.
    97	 *
    98	 * **Ante un error PARA y no reanuda.** Es deliberado y no es pereza: una
    99	 * longitud fuera de rango o una etiqueta desconocida significan que el flujo
   100	 * perdió la sincronía, y a partir de ahí no hay forma de saber dónde empieza
   101	 * la trama siguiente — seguir leyendo produciría tramas inventadas a partir
   102	 * de bytes que son la mitad de otra cosa. Callar el error y seguir es peor
   103	 * que parar: entrega datos que parecen válidos.
   104	 *
   105	 * Rendimiento: guarda un solo `Buffer` de bytes pendientes entre llamadas, con
   106	 * un `concat` por trozo. Es O(n) por trama y suficiente para el tráfico de un
   107	 * PTY; si algún día el perfil lo señalara, la forma es una cola de trozos con
   108	 * lectura por índice en vez de la concatenación.
   109	 */
   110	export function createFrameDecoder(
   111	  onFrame: (f: DecodedFrame) => void,
   112	  onError: (msg: string) => void,
   113	): (chunk: Buffer) => void {
   114	  let pending = Buffer.alloc(0)
   115	  let stopped = false
   116	
   117	  return (chunk: Buffer) => {
   118	    if (stopped) return
   119	    pending = pending.length === 0 ? Buffer.from(chunk) : Buffer.concat([pending, chunk])
   120	
   121	    while (pending.length >= FRAME_HEADER_BYTES) {
   122	      const len = pending.readUInt32BE(0)
   123	      if (len > FRAME_SIZE_CAP) {
   124	        stopped = true
   125	        onError(`frame too large (${len} > ${FRAME_SIZE_CAP})`)
   126	        return
   127	      }

    93	  })

   114	      () => {},
   115	      () => {
   116	        connected = true
   117	      },
   118	    )

   120	    expect(connected).toBe(true)
   121	    // No reply was enqueued by the handshake.
   122	    expect(replies).toEqual([])
   123	    client.close()
   124	  })

   127	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   128	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   129	    await startRendezvousServer({ isRendererReady: () => true })

   132	    let connected = false
   133	    const client = createRvClient(

   148	    expect(received.some(m => m.type === 'heartbeat')).toBe(true)
   149	    client.close()
   150	  })

   153	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   154	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   155	    await startRendezvousServer({ isRendererReady: () => true })
   156	
   157	    let connected = false
   158	    let disconnects = 0
   159	    const client = createRvClient(
   160	      sock,
   161	      () => {},
   162	      () => {
   163	        disconnects++
   164	      },
   165	      () => {
   166	        connected = true
   167	      },
   168	    )
   169	    await until(() => connected)
   170	    // Tearing the server down drops the live connection → onDisconnect.
   171	    stopRendezvousServer()
   172	    await until(() => disconnects > 0)
   173	    expect(disconnects).toBeGreaterThan(0)
   174	    client.close()
   175	  })
   176	
   177	  test('supervisor reply reaches the worker enqueueReply hook', async () => {
   178	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   179	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   180	    const replies: string[] = []
   181	    await startRendezvousServer({
   182	      enqueueReply: t => replies.push(t),
   183	      isRendererReady: () => true,
   184	    })
   185	
   186	    let connected = false
   187	    const client = createRvClient(
   188	      sock,
   189	      () => {},
   190	      () => {},
   191	      () => {
   192	        connected = true
   193	      },
   194	    )
   195	    await until(() => connected)
   196	    expect(client.send({ type: 'reply', text: 'continue please' })).toBe(true)
   197	    await until(() => replies.length > 0)
   198	    expect(replies).toEqual(['continue please'])
   199	    client.close()
   200	  })
   201	
   202	  test('reply answering an open question short-circuits enqueue', async () => {
   203	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   204	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   205	    const replies: string[] = []
   206	    await startRendezvousServer({
   207	      enqueueReply: t => replies.push(t),
   208	      answersOpenQuestion: t => t === 'yes',
   209	      isRendererReady: () => true,
   210	    })
   211	    let connected = false
   212	    const client = createRvClient(
   213	      sock,
   214	      () => {},
   215	      () => {},
   216	      () => {
   217	        connected = true
   218	      },
   219	    )
   220	    await until(() => connected)
   221	    client.send({ type: 'reply', text: 'yes' })
   222	    // Give the frame time to land; it should NOT enqueue.
   223	    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100))
   224	    expect(replies).toEqual([])
   225	    client.close()
   226	  })
   227	
   228	  test('supervisor repaint triggers forceRedraw + repaint-done ack', async () => {
   229	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   230	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   231	    let redrawCount = 0
   232	    await startRendezvousServer({
   233	      forceRedraw: () => {
   234	        redrawCount++
   235	        return true
   236	      },
   237	      isRendererReady: () => true,
   238	    })
   239	    const received: RvServerMessage[] = []
   240	    let connected = false
   241	    const client = createRvClient(
   242	      sock,
   243	      m => received.push(m),
   244	      () => {},
   245	      () => {
   246	        connected = true
   247	      },
   248	    )
   249	    await until(() => connected)
   250	    client.send({ type: 'repaint' })
   251	    await until(() => received.some(m => m.type === 'repaint-done'))
   252	    expect(redrawCount).toBe(1)
   253	    expect(received.some(m => m.type === 'repaint-done')).toBe(true)
   254	    client.close()
   255	  })
   256	
   257	  test('shutdown frame acks shutting-down + calls onShutdown', async () => {
   258	    const sock = freshSockPath()
   259	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   260	    let shutdownCalled = false
   261	    await startRendezvousServer({
   262	      onShutdown: () => {
   263	        shutdownCalled = true
   264	      },
   265	      isRendererReady: () => true,
   266	    })
   267	    const received: RvServerMessage[] = []
   268	    let connected = false
   269	    const client = createRvClient(
   270	      sock,
   271	      m => received.push(m),
   272	      () => {},
   273	      () => {
   274	        connected = true
   275	      },
   276	    )

   282	    // message has already crossed the Unix socket.
   283	    await until(

   298	    const first = createRvClient(
   299	      sock,
   300	      () => {},
   301	      () => {},
   302	      () => {
   303	        firstConnected = true
   304	      },
   305	    )

   307

   309	    const second = createRvClient(

   311	      () => {},
   312	      () => {},
   313	      () => {

   315	      },

   331	    process.env.THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK = sock
   332	    process.env.THYROX_JOB_DIR = jobDir
   333	    // Seed a baseline state.json so pushRvState has something to merge.
   334	    const { writeJobState, readJobState } = await import(
   335	      '@thyrox/agent/background/fleet/fleetStore.js'
   336	    )
   337	    const now = new Date().toISOString()
   338	    await writeJobState(jobDir, {
   339	      state: 'working',
   340	      tempo: 'active',
   341	      detail: 'seed',
   342	      output: null,
   343	      children: null,
   344	      linkScanOffset: 0,
   345	      template: 'bg',
   346	      respawnFlags: [],
   347	      intent: 'do a thing',
   348	      sessionId: '',
   349	      daemonShort: 'state01',
   350	      cwd: jobDir,
   351	      createdAt: now,
   352	      updatedAt: now,
   353	      firstTerminalAt: null,
   354	      backend: 'daemon',
   355	    })
   356	    await startRendezvousServer({ isRendererReady: () => true })
   357	
   358	    const received: RvServerMessage[] = []
   359	    let connected = false
   360	    const client = createRvClient(
   361	      sock,
   362	      m => received.push(m),
   363	      () => {},
   364	      () => {
   365	        connected = true
   366	      },
   367	    )
   368	    await until(() => connected)
   369	
   370	    await pushRvState({ state: 'done', tempo: 'idle', detail: 'finished' })
   371	    await until(() => received.some(m => m.type === 'state'))
   372	
   373	    // Disk reflects the merged patch.
   374	    const onDisk = await readJobState(jobDir)
   375	    expect(onDisk?.state).toBe('done')

   381	    const statePush = received.find(m => m.type === 'state') as

   383	      | undefined
   384	    expect(statePush?.patch.state).toBe('done')
   385	    client.close()
   386	  })
   387	})

describe('rv channel — malformed line resilience', () => {
  /**
   * Raw `node:net` server instead of the fleet rvServer fixture: this test
   * needs wire-level control (write an invalid JSON line, then a valid one)
   * that `sendRv`'s typed API doesn't expose.
   *
   * Reference: chunk-ygx717jg.js `Be` composes `Zzt` (chunk-y641zpzf.js,
   * newline-frame reader) with an inline `try{P=J(A)}catch{return}` per
   * line — one malformed line is dropped silently and the connection stays
   * open for the next line. `rvClient.ts` used to hand the whole stream to
   * `socketProto.ts::createLineDecoder`, whose `onError` is wired to
   * `sock.destroy()` for ANY parse failure — worse coverage than the
   * reference, which only loses that one line.
   */
  test('a malformed JSON line is dropped; the connection and later valid frames survive', async () => {
    const { createServer } = await import('node:net')
    const sock = freshSockPath()
    let rawSocket: import('node:net').Socket | undefined
    const server = createServer(s => {
      rawSocket = s
      // Discard the handshake line (role marker) — nothing to do with it here.
    })
    await new Promise<void>(resolve => server.listen(sock, resolve))

    const received: RvServerMessage[] = []
    let connected = false
    const client = createRvClient(
      sock,
      m => received.push(m),
      () => {},
      () => {
        connected = true
      },
    )
    await until(() => connected)
    await until(() => rawSocket !== undefined)

    rawSocket!.write('not-json-at-all\n')
    rawSocket!.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'heartbeat' })}\n`)

    await until(() => received.some(m => m.type === 'heartbeat'))
    expect(received.filter(m => m.type === 'heartbeat').length).toBe(1)
    expect(received.length).toBe(1)

    client.close()
    server.close()
  })
})
EOF

/**
 * Protocolo de claim del spare pool — puerto de `chunk-ygx717jg.js`
 * (ant 4644.js) `xt`, `Bt`, `Ft`, `Ut`, `P9n` y `O9n`.
 *
 * `sparePool.ts` reserva el slot (quién puede reclamar qué); este archivo
 * es el CABLE: arma la trama de claim, la envía con reintento y
 * presupuesto, y limpia el socket del repuesto cuando el envío falla del
 * todo. `bgDaemon.ts` es el único llamador (bloque de claim en `dispatch`
 * + scheduler de prewarm).
 *
 * Divergencia estructural declarada: la referencia usa DOS sockets por
 * repuesto — un `ptySock` (E/S normal) y un `claimSock` efímero, sólo
 * vivo mientras el repuesto espera claim, con su propio receptor
 * autenticado (`Kjt`/`AVo`, ver abajo). `@thyrox/daemon` no tiene ese
 * segundo socket: reutiliza el `ptySock` del repuesto (ya bindeado por
 * `spawnPtyHost`) para todo, incluida la trama de claim. El protocolo de
 * cable de `Ft`/`Ut` (JSON + salto de línea sobre el `claimSock`) se porta
 * aquí ADAPTADO al framing binario que `@thyrox/daemon` ya usa en el
 * `ptySock` (`internal/ptyFrame.ts::encodeCtrlFrame`), no verbatim.
 *
 * Pendiente, declarado y no silenciado:
 *  - `AVo` (entrypoint del proceso hijo `--bg-spare` que escucha el
 *    `claimSock` autenticado) no existe: no hay hoy un modo `--bg-spare`
 *    real en `@thyrox/daemon`/`@thyrox/cli`, así que no hay receptor que
 *    verifique `auth`. La trama SÍ lleva `auth` (ver `buildSpareClaimFrame`)
 *    pero nada del lado del repuesto la comprueba todavía.
 *  - `Kjt`/`Yjt` (recepción autenticada del claim + bootstrap post-claim
 *    del REPL) — mismo motivo, ausentes.
 *  - `I9n` (refill con jerarquía `bg-pty-host` → `--bg-spare`, detección
 *    OOM/cgroup vs fork-and-exit del lanzador, `discardSpentCredentialFile`)
 *    — `bgDaemon.ts` spawnea el repuesto directo vía `spawnPtyHost`, sin
 *    esa jerarquía ni esa clasificación de fallo; sólo se porta aquí la
 *    mitad de `I9n` que es de este archivo: el hueco mínimo de refill tras
 *    un exit (`SPARE_REFILL_MIN_GAP_MS`, en `sparePool.ts`) y la vigilancia
 *    de orfandad por ppid (`startPpidWatchdog`, lista para cuando exista
 *    un entrypoint `--bg-spare` real que la invoque).
 */

import { readdir, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { connect, type Socket } from 'node:net'
import { platform as osPlatform } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'

import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'

    14	 *     `Oe`=30 attempts (`PTY_MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`).

   107	    .slice(0, 2000)
   108	    .split(/\r?\n/)
   109	    .map(line => line.trim())

   111	}

   115	 * also a prefix of `needle`, used to hold back a sentinel match that
   116	 * straddles a chunk boundary. Byte-for-byte the same algorithm as

   119	 * the same boundary `internal/ptyFrame.ts` already duplicates).
   120	 */
   121	export function suffixMatchLen(buf: Buffer, needle: Buffer): number {
   122	  const max = Math.min(buf.length, needle.length - 1)

   124	    const start = buf.length - k

   126	      if (buf[start + i] !== needle[i]) continue outer

   128	    return k
   129	  }

   135	  signal?: string

   154	  onExit: (info: WorkerExitInfo) => void
   155	  onHeartbeat?: (info: { ts: number; state?: string }) => void

   167	  replVersion(): string

   179	  if (pid <= 1) return false
   180	  try {
   181	    process.kill(pid, 0)
   182	    return true
   183	  } catch (e) {
   184	    return (e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EPERM'

   191	  } catch {
   192	    try {
   193	      process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL')
   194	    } catch {
   195	      // best-effort — the process is already gone.
   196	    }
   197	  }
   198	}

   202	 * a pure codec (encode only, on purpose — see its own docstring) and
   203	 * isn't ours to extend with a decoder. Same wire shape as
   204	 * `@thyrox/cli: bg/ptyFrame.ts::createFrameDecoder`, ported independently
   205	 * because the two packages don't share a dependency edge (same reason
   206	 * `internal/ptyFrame.ts` itself is a duplicate, not an import).
   207	 */
   208	function createDaemonFrameDecoder(
   209	  onFrame: (f: DecodedFrame) => void,
   210	  onError: (msg: string) => void,
   211	): (chunk: Buffer) => void {
   212	  let pending = Buffer.alloc(0)
   213	  let stopped = false
   214	  return (chunk: Buffer) => {
   215	    if (stopped) return
   216	    pending = pending.length === 0 ? Buffer.from(chunk) : Buffer.concat([pending, chunk])
   217	    while (pending.length >= FRAME_HEADER_BYTES) {
   218	      const len = pending.readUInt32BE(0)

   220	        stopped = true
   221	        onError(`frame too large (${len} > ${FRAME_SIZE_CAP})`)
   222	        return
   223	      }

   225	      if (pending.length < total) return
   226	      const tag = pending.readUInt8(4)
   227	      const body = pending.subarray(FRAME_HEADER_BYTES, total)
   228	      pending = pending.subarray(total)

   230	        onFrame({ kind: DATA_TAG, payload: Buffer.from(body) })
   231	      } else if (tag === CTRL_TAG) {
   232	        try {
   233	          const ctrl = JSON.parse(body.toString('utf8')) as CtrlFrame
   234	          onFrame({ kind: CTRL_TAG, ctrl })
   235	        } catch {
   236	          stopped = true
   237	          onError('bad ctrl frame json')
   238	          return
   239	        }
   240	      } else {
   241	        stopped = true
   242	        onError(`unknown frame tag ${tag}`)
   243	        return
   244	      }
   245	    }
   246	  }
   247	}
